delete.description:
Irreversible, unlike archiving a ticket. Private saved views go with the account - nobody else could see them, and left behind they would be owned by nobody and visible to nobody. Shared views stay with the team, now ownerless. Comments and ticket assignments keep their rows and lose their name: work outlives the people who touched it.

Only your own account. Deleting someone else's would need an authority model this schema does not define.

post.description:
Public: this is how a person gets a session. Creates the account and, in the same transaction, its membership of the workspace - creating the workspace first if the install has none. On success it sets the session cookie exactly as login does.

Single-workspace model: when a workspace already exists the new account joins it as a member. There is no invitation or approval step yet (ADR 0004), so until there is, anyone who can reach this endpoint can join - do not expose it beyond a trusted network.

A duplicate email answers 409 `email_taken`. That reveals the address is registered, which a registration endpoint cannot avoid; it costs the same time as a success.
post.summary: Create an account and log in as it

post.description: Send `Idempotency-Key` to make the create safe to retry after a lost response. The first request with a key creates the ticket and answers `Idempotent-Replayed: false`; any later request with the same key from the same account creates nothing and answers `Idempotent-Replayed: true` with the original ticket as it is now - same status, 200, as a fresh create. A replay publishes nothing on the change feed. If the original has been archived the answer is a 409 `ticket_archived` carrying it. The body of a replay is ignored.

parameters.description: Makes the create safe to retry. The same key from the same account returns the ticket the first call created instead of creating another - the original's current state, with Idempotent-Replayed: true. 1 to 128 printable ASCII characters; a UUID is ideal. Keys are per account and never expire. A replay ignores the body it carries: send a new key for a different ticket. Omit it for a plain create.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: Makes the create safe to retry. The same key from the same account returns the ticket the first call created instead of creating another - the original's current state, with Idempotent-Replayed: true. 1 to 128 printable ASCII characters; a UUID is ideal. Keys are per account and never expire. A replay ignores the body it carries: send a new key for a different ticket. Omit it for a plain create.
The ticket's version in quotes, as If-Match takes it back.
Only when Idempotency-Key was sent. true: that key had been used, nothing was created, and the body is the original ticket as it is now. false: this request created the ticket.

409.description: Conflict. Only when Idempotency-Key was sent and had already created a ticket that has since been archived: code is ticket_archived, current is that ticket and changed_by and changed_at say who archived it and when. Nothing was written, and no second ticket exists - restore the original or discard the local copy.

post.summary: Create a ticket (safe to retry with Idempotency-Key)

delete.description: Takes `If-Match` like the update does. A ticket that is already archived answers `ticket_archived` when `If-Match` is sent - including when the archive was your own and the response was lost, in which case `changed_by` is you - and `ticket_not_found` when it is not. The ticket's new version is in the `ETag` header.

parameters.description: Make the write conditional on the ticket still being at the version you last saw, written as the ETag is: the number in double quotes, for example "4". If the ticket has moved on the write is refused with a 409 and nothing changes: ticket_conflict if it was edited, ticket_archived if it was archived - each carrying the current copy, who changed it and when. Omit it for a plain last-write-wins write.
parameters.name: If-Match

schema.description: Make the write conditional on the ticket still being at the version you last saw, written as the ETag is: the number in double quotes, for example "4". 409.description: Conflict. Only when If-Match was sent: code is ticket_conflict if the ticket was edited since that version, ticket_archived if it was archived. Nothing was written.

put.description: Last write wins unless `If-Match` is sent. With `If-Match: "<version>"` the write happens only if the ticket is still at that version; otherwise it is refused with a 409 (`ticket_conflict` or `ticket_archived`) that carries the current ticket, who changed it and when. Without it, a write to an archived ticket is `ticket_not_found`, as it always was.
